edits.original: We did a bunch of tests to check whether the treatment worked.
edits.revised: We performed a series of assays to determine whether the treatment was effective.
edits.reason: 'did a bunch of tests' and 'worked' are colloquial; they are replaced with formal academic equivalents.
edits.basis: Academic register guideline: avoid colloquial quantifiers ('a bunch of') and vague verbs ('worked').

edits.original: These results prove that the new protocol is perfect for all cell types.
edits.revised: These results suggest that the new protocol is effective for the cell types tested.
edits.reason: 'prove' and 'perfect for all cell types' claim more than the data support; the claim is hedged to match the evidence scope.
edits.basis: Hedging guideline: claim strength must match the strength and scope of the evidence.

edits.original: Due to the fact that the signal was weak at this point in time, the exposure time was increased to 30 s.
edits.revised: Because the signal was weak, the exposure time was increased to 30 s.
edits.reason: 'Due to the fact that' and 'at this point in time' are redundant wordy phrases replaced by concise equivalents without meaning change.
edits.basis: Conciseness rule: replace multi-word connectives with single-word equivalents when meaning is unchanged.

edits.original: The samples were heated to 95 °C for 10 min then cooled on ice.
edits.revised: The samples were heated to 95 °C for 10 min, then cooled on ice.
edits.reason: A comma is required before 'then' when it links two sequential actions in one sentence.
edits.basis: Comma rule: use a comma before the conjunctive adverb 'then' joining sequential clauses.

edits.original: Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05, and representative images are shown in Fig. 2.
edits.revised: Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05, with representative images in Fig. 2.

edits.original: Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05, and representative images are shown in Fig. 2.
edits.revised: Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05; representative images are shown in Fig. 2.
edits.reason: A semicolon tightens the link between two closely related independent clauses here.
edits.basis: Semicolon rule: a semicolon may join two closely related independent clauses without a conjunction.
